name: King Henry VI
description: The gentle, devout king, now grown but no stronger, who marries Margaret of Anjou and looks on helplessly as his uncle Gloucester is destroyed, his court splinters into factions, and the Duke of York's claim hardens into open war. He would rather be a subject than a king.

name: Queen Margaret
description: Henry's French queen, brought to England by the infatuated Suffolk, with whom she conducts a barely-veiled affair. Contemptuous of her weak husband and of 'good Duke Humphrey,' she emerges as a fierce political player; she cradles the severed head of the murdered Suffolk.

name: Duke of Gloucester
description: Humphrey, Duke of Gloucester, the Lord Protector — 'good Duke Humphrey' — the honest anchor of the realm and the commons' darling. Undone by his wife's witchcraft and his enemies' conspiracies, he is stripped of office, arrested, and murdered in his bed at Bury St Edmunds.

name: Eleanor, Duchess of Gloucester
description: Eleanor Cobham, Gloucester's ambitious wife, who dreams of the crown and dabbles in witchcraft, employing a priest, a conjurer, and a witch to raise a prophesying spirit. Caught, she does humiliating public penance through the London streets and is banished, pulling her husband down with her.

name: Duke of Suffolk
description: William de la Pole, Duke of Suffolk, the queen's lover and the architect of Gloucester's fall. Banished for the murder, he is captured at sea and beheaded by a pirate crew who scorn his pride; his head is sent back to the grieving Margaret.

name: Richard, Duke of York
description: Richard Plantagenet, Duke of York, who lays out his hereditary claim to the crown in soliloquy, secretly foments Jack Cade's rebellion as a trial of strength, and finally returns from Ireland with an army — opening the Wars of the Roses at the first battle of St Albans.

name: Cardinal Beaufort
description: Cardinal Beaufort, Bishop of Winchester, Gloucester's great-uncle and bitter enemy, who engineers the Protector's arrest and murder. Tormented by guilt, he dies raving and grasping at the air, signing for mercy he cannot ask.

name: Earl of Warwick
description: Richard Neville, Earl of Warwick — the future 'Kingmaker' — who proves from the corpse that Gloucester was strangled and rallies the commons against Suffolk. He throws in his lot with York at St Albans.

name: Earl of Salisbury
description: Richard Neville, Earl of Salisbury, Warwick's father, a respected elder peer who comes to accept York's title and joins the Yorkist cause.

name: Duke of Buckingham
description: A loyal Lancastrian peer sent to disperse Cade's rebels with a royal pardon and to treat with the returning York.

name: Duke of Somerset
description: York's rival, blamed for the loss of France; York makes Somerset's removal his price for peace, and at St Albans Young Clifford and the Yorkists hunt him down.

name: Lord Clifford
description: A staunch Lancastrian lord who helps disperse Cade's rebels and is slain by York at the first battle of St Albans, igniting his son's vow of revenge.

name: Young Clifford
description: Finding his father's body at St Albans, he swears pitiless vengeance on the house of York — 'York not our old men spares; no more will I their babes' — foreshadowing the savagery of the sequels.

name: Jack Cade
description: The Kentish rebel, secretly set on by York, who claims descent from the Mortimers and leads a bloody, anti-literate uprising — promising seven halfpenny loaves for a penny and the death of all lawyers. His mob takes London before deserting him; he is killed, starving, in Iden's garden.

name: Dick the Butcher
description: Cade's brutal lieutenant, who utters the rebellion's most famous line: 'The first thing we do, let's kill all the lawyers.'

name: Smith the Weaver
description: One of Cade's followers, given to dry asides that puncture his leader's grand claims.

name: John Holland
description: A commoner who joins Cade's rebellion, lamenting that honest tradesmen have fallen on hard times.

name: George Bevis
description: One of Cade's rebel band from the Kentish commons.

name: Michael
description: Cade's follower who brings word that Sir Humphrey Stafford and the King's forces are near.

name: Lord Say
description: Lord Say, the learned royal treasurer, condemned by Cade for the crimes of building a grammar school and using printed paper; he is beheaded and his head paraded on a pole.

name: Lord Scales
description: Commander of the Tower of London, who holds it against Cade's rebels and sends Matthew Goffe to fight them in the city.

name: Sir Humphrey Stafford
description: A royal officer sent with his brother to crush Cade; both are killed, and Cade mockingly wears Stafford's armor.

name: William Stafford
description: Sir Humphrey Stafford's brother, killed beside him by Cade's rebels.

name: Alexander Iden
description: A contented Kentish squire who, walking in his garden, kills the starving fugitive Cade and is knighted for carrying his head to the King.

name: Walter Whitmore
description: The pirate who claims Suffolk as his prize and beheads him, fulfilling a prophecy that Suffolk should die 'by water' (Walter).

name: Sea-Captain
description: Captain of the pirate ship that takes Suffolk, who denounces the duke's crimes before handing him to Whitmore.

name: Peter Thump
description: Thomas Horner's apprentice, who accuses his master of saying York is the rightful king; the dispute is settled by a judicial duel, which the drunken Horner loses.

name: Thomas Horner
description: An armorer accused of treason by his apprentice Peter; he is killed in their trial by combat, confessing as he dies.

name: Saunder Simpcox
description: An impostor who pretends to have been born blind and miraculously cured at St Alban's shrine; Gloucester exposes the fraud by proving he could not name colors he claims only just to have seen, then has him whipped.

name: Simpcox's Wife
description: Simpcox's wife, who pleads that poverty, not malice, drove the false miracle.

name: John Hume
description: A corrupt priest who arranges the conjuring for the Duchess while secretly in the pay of her enemies, the Cardinal and Suffolk.

name: Roger Bolingbroke
description: A conjurer (NOT the usurping king of Richard II) who, at the Duchess of Gloucester's bidding, raises a spirit to prophesy the fates of the King and the great lords; he is taken in the act and executed.

name: Margery Jourdain
description: A witch who assists the conjuring of the spirit for the Duchess; she is condemned to be burned at Smithfield.

name: Spirit (Asnath)
description: The fiend raised by the conjuring, which answers in riddling prophecies — that the King shall be deposed by one who 'shall depose,' and that Suffolk shall die by water — before being dismissed back to hell.

name: Richard Plantagenet
description: York's deformed youngest son — the future Richard III — who fights for his father at St Albans and kills Somerset there.

name: Edward Plantagenet
description: York's eldest son, the future Edward IV, who joins the Yorkist victory at St Albans.

name: Sir John Stanley
description: The officer charged with escorting the banished Duchess of Gloucester to her imprisonment on the Isle of Man.

name: Vaux
description: A messenger who brings word that the Cardinal lies dying and raving.

name: Beadle
description: The officer who whips the impostor Simpcox out of St Alban's.

name: Clerk of Chartham
description: A literate clerk whom Cade's rebels hang for the crime of being able to read and write his own name.
